title: A heritable label in the fuel-powered CIPS cells: two variants of a label the body copies with its own catalysis stay pure through division and change whether the body divides
summary: World: c48's fuel-powered-turnover CIPS cells plus two variants g1, g2 of a label copied autocatalytically by the body's own catalysis (kg cat g_k (1-g1-g2), so copying needs fuel), held inside bodies by the TOOLBOX min-gated sealed mobility (inside = e>0.5) with fast decay outside; g2 multiplies the body's catalysis by (1 + a2 g2). On seed 0 each body was inoculated at t=1500 with g1 or g2 by a fair coin (6 g1, 2 g2); to t=10000 every body stays pure (g of its kind 0.99, the other 0.00; 0 impure of 16-19) and every daughter carries its parent's kind. With a2=-0.3 the 2 g2 bodies never elongate or divide (area flat at about 205 px) while the g1 bodies go 6 -> 14; with a2=+0.3 g2 goes 2 -> 6 and g1 6 -> 12. Kinds were assigned at seeding and the seal is a written gate, so this is a heredity test, not selection; a run with trait-blind swap mutations, trait-blind washout and an a2=0 twin is under way.
